results.title: Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion
results.abstract: Inference-time scaling has become the dominant lever for improving language-model reasoning, but existing methods often derive rollout diversity from a single source: stochastic token-level sampling. We identify a second, fully \emph{deterministic} and \emph{complementary} axis: the layer span $L$ at which a frozen model's top decoder layers are recursively re-applied at high-uncertainty tokens. Different choices of $L$ produce distinct rollouts that solve different subsets of problems, with no stochasticity. We instantiate this axis through \emph{Entropy-Gated Latent Recursion} (EGLR), a training-free decoding procedure that, combined with temperature sampling, turns a single-axis rollout pool into an $L\!\times\!T$ Cartesian sampling space at almost the same per-rollout cost. Across $8$ instruction-tuned models and $6$ math benchmarks, majority voting over the $L$ axis matches or improves on greedy decoding in nearly all settings and outperforms FLOP-matched beam search, and the gains carry over to a code benchmark. On MATH-500, the oracle ceiling of the joint pool exceeds that of either axis alone by $8$ to $10$ points. In a preliminary study, using the pool for GRPO rollouts with importance-sampling correction improves over standard GRPO. The code is available at \href{https://github.com/spotai-mbzuai/neurips26-eglr}{https://github.com/spotai-mbzuai/eglr}.
